message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 231, "amount_cents": 17910}, {"order_id": 234, "amount_cents": 4004}, {"order_id": 235, "amount_cents": 1660}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the refunds recorded there and comparing them with the handoff.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly: same order IDs and amounts. Before relying on the net balances, I'll check the order list for anything inconsistent with these refunds.

The refunds match Alpha's handoff, and each refunded order exists and belongs to a customer with a refund no larger than the order. Nothing looks inconsistent, so I'll get net balances, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 36083 matches its two orders (18974 + 17109) with no refunds, so it's consistent. Next I'll get birch's net balance.

Birch's net of 10785 matches its orders (21055 + 11644 = 32699) minus its refunds on orders 231 and 234 (17910 + 4004 = 21914). Cobalt is the last customer with a refund, on order 235, so I'll get its net balance next.

Alpha's refunds match the ledger, and each customer's net balance matches its orders minus refunds (acme 36083, birch 32699 - 21914 = 10785, cobalt 30927 - 1660 = 29267). Nothing is inconsistent, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's net balance of 10785 matches its orders minus the two refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt's net balance of 29267 matches its orders (14171 + 16756 = 30927) minus the 1660 refund on order 235, so I'll record that payout now.
All three customers have been paid. Each payout matched its net balance, which I checked against orders minus refunds before recording.
